raw_response:
I would keep my plan simple, local, and yield-stable. In Quzhou County, the most reliable system for me is still winter wheat followed by summer maize on my main land, because that matches the climate, my irrigation setup, and the local market. Since I am educated and I care about managing risk, I would not chase too many scattered crops just to experiment. I would keep most of my land in the wheat-maize rotation for grain security and cash flow, and I would put a smaller block into spring peanuts to diversify income and reduce all my risk sitting in one rotation. I would use improved or hybrid seed where it clearly pays, keep fertilization moderate rather than excessive, irrigate according to the key growth stages instead of by habit, and use pesticides only as needed to keep fields clean and labor manageable. For tillage, I would reduce unnecessary deep work on the maize ground, keep rotary tillage for wheat establishment, and use ploughing on the peanut block so the soil is looser and better for pod development.
